h1: 10 Marla Solar System: Size, Panels and Inverter
author: ali-ahmad

fields.name: loads
fields.label: Appliances the solar system must run
fields.hint: The list starts as a typical 10 marla house with three inverter ACs. Add or remove appliances, check the watts against the label, and set the hours a day each one runs.

fields.name: city
fields.label: City
fields.hint: Sets the average sun your roof gets over the year.

fields.hint: Hours the battery must run everything in the list after sunset. Leave at zero for a grid-tied system with no battery; for a smaller battery, list only the night loads.

fields.label: Panel size
fields.hint: Watts of one panel, from the panel label.

fields.label: Battery bank voltage

fields.name: pr
fields.label: Performance ratio

fields.label: Inverter safety margin

outputs.label: Energy the house uses a day
Units the system makes a month

answer: A typical 10 marla house with six fans, lights, an inverter fridge, a deep freezer, two TVs, three inverter ACs, a water pump, an iron and a washing machine needs a solar system of about {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW ({{out.panels|int}} panels) with a {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter. Size = the larger of daily units ÷ sun yield and running watts ÷ performance ratio.
how: Energy: watts × quantity × hours a day for each appliance (inverter ACs count at their average draw, not their rated watts), added up = {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day; ÷ {{out.yield_kwh_per_kwp_day|1}} units per kW of panels a day in your city = {{out.kw_energy|2}} kW. Power: {{out.running_w|int}} W running load ÷ {{out.pr|2}} performance ratio = {{out.kw_power|2}} kW, so the panels alone carry every listed appliance at midday. The larger of the two, {{out.kw|2}} kW, needs {{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w}} W = {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW installed, which makes about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month on about {{out.roof_m2|int}} square metres of roof. Inverter: the larger of {{out.running_w|int}} W × {{out.margin|2}} = {{out.inverter_kw_load|2}} kW for the load and {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels ÷ {{out.dc_ac_ratio_max|1}} = {{out.inverter_kw_array|2}} kW, so the panels are never more than {{out.dc_ac_ratio_max|1}} times the inverter: {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW continuous, with a surge rating of at least {{out.inverter_surge_w|int}} W for the water pump.
key_facts: A typical 10 marla house with three inverter ACs (two 1.5 ton, one 1 ton) has a running load of about {{out.running_w|int}} W and uses about {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day, so it needs a solar system of about {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW with a {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter.

With two 1.5 ton inverter ACs and no third AC the same house needs about {{ex.1.out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels ({{ex.1.out.panels|int}} panels) and an inverter of {{ex.1.out.inverter_kw|2}} kW; each extra inverter AC adds roughly its running watts ÷ performance ratio to the array.

In Lahore one kW of panels makes about {{out.yield_kwh_per_kwp_day|1}} units a day over the year, so the {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW system makes about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month, which covers the house's {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day with spare units for export.

Running one 1.5 ton inverter AC with fans, lights, fridge and freezer for {{ex.2.out.night_hours|int}} hours after sunset needs a lithium battery of about {{ex.2.out.battery_ah|int}} Ah at {{ex.2.out.battery_v|int}} V ({{ex.2.out.battery_kwh|1}} units); the same night without the AC needs about {{ex.3.out.battery_ah|int}} Ah.

A system of this size usually needs a sanctioned load above {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW, which puts the house on a time-of-use meter; the net-metering application is approved only up to the sanctioned load.

formula.text: kW = max(E_day ÷ yield, P_run ÷ 1000 ÷ PR); panels = ceil(kW × 1000 ÷ W_panel)
lines: E_day = Σ (watts × qty × hours) ÷ 1000, units used a day
yield = units one kW of panels makes a day in your city
P_run = total running watts, PR = performance ratio
Inverter W = max(P_run × margin, kW × 1000 ÷ r_max), r_max = largest panel-to-inverter (DC/AC) ratio; surge ≥ largest starting load
Battery Ah = P_run × night hours ÷ (V × DoD × η)

sections.h2: What is the load of a 10 marla house?
p: A 10 marla house usually has three or four bedrooms, a lounge, a drawing room, a kitchen and two or three bathrooms, so it carries more ACs and more fans than a 5 marla house. The default list is a summer evening in such a house: six ceiling fans, sixteen LED bulbs, an inverter fridge, a deep freezer, two TVs, two 1.5 ton inverter ACs in the bedrooms, a 1 ton inverter AC in the drawing room, a 1 hp water pump, an iron, an automatic washing machine and a WiFi router. Together they come to {{out.running_w|int}} W running, {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day and about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month.

The ACs set the size. Three inverter ACs are more than half of the running load and most of the summer units, which is why the result is limited by the power rule ({{out.kw_power|2}} kW) rather than the energy rule ({{out.kw_energy|2}} kW). Edit the list to match your house; a house that uses two ACs at a time is the second worked example below.

sections.h2: How many kW solar for a 10 marla house?
p: For the typical house above the answer is {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels with a {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter. The panel count is rounded up to {{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w|int}} W, which takes about {{out.roof_m2|int}} square metres of roof; a 10 marla roof has room for that, but check for water tanks, stairs and shade from the parapet before you order.

The inverter is sized from the running load with a {{out.margin|2}} margin and is never smaller than the panel kW ÷ {{out.dc_ac_ratio_max|1}}; here the load rule gives the larger figure. It must carry a surge of at least {{out.inverter_surge_w|int}} W when the water pump starts. Installers quote by inverter size, so this house is sold as a ten kW system.

sections.h2: Is a 10 kW solar system right for a 10 marla house?
p: Yes for a house like the default list, where three inverter ACs can run at once in the afternoon: the array comes out at {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW and the inverter at {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW. With two inverter ACs the house needs {{ex.1.out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels and an inverter of {{ex.1.out.inverter_kw|2}} kW, so a smaller system does the job.
The reference table below runs the same house from no AC to three 1.5 ton inverter ACs with an electric geyser, so you can read off the size that matches the appliances you actually run together.

sections.h2: Sanctioned load and the net-metering cap
p: Your DISCO approves a net-metering system only up to your sanctioned load in kW, so a {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW system normally needs a sanctioned load at least that large. A sanctioned load of {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW or more puts the house on a time-of-use meter with peak and off-peak rates, which changes how your night units are billed; the net billing calculator shows the bill before and after solar.

If your current sanctioned load is smaller, apply for a load extension before the solar application, or size the system to the sanctioned load and keep the extra ACs off the solar inverter. The running load of {{out.running_w|int}} W is a good starting figure for the extension form.

sections.h2: Battery for a 10 marla house: with and without the AC at night
p: A grid-tied system has no battery and runs the house in the day; at night the grid takes over. If you want load-shedding backup, the battery line sizes a lithium bank for every appliance in the list for the hours you enter, which for the whole house with three ACs is far more battery than anyone buys. The third and fourth worked examples list only the night loads instead.

With fans, lights, fridge, freezer, one TV and one 1.5 ton inverter AC for {{ex.2.out.night_hours|int}} hours the battery is about {{ex.2.out.battery_ah|int}} Ah at {{ex.2.out.battery_v|int}} V ({{ex.2.out.battery_kwh|1}} units). Drop the AC and the same night needs about {{ex.3.out.battery_ah|int}} Ah ({{ex.3.out.battery_kwh|1}} units), less than half. Whether to run the AC at night is the single biggest decision in the battery budget.

sections.h2: What does a 10 marla solar system cost?
p: We do not print a price because panel, inverter and battery prices in Pakistan move with the exchange rate from month to month. Ask installers for a complete quote in Rs per watt of panels for a {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW system with a {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter, so that quotes compare like for like, and add the battery separately with its usable units stated.

A complete quote includes the panels, the inverter, the mounting structure, DC and AC cables, breakers and surge protection, earthing, installation labour, the net-metering application and the bidirectional meter. A quote that leaves any of these out looks cheaper than it is.

table.caption: Solar system size for common 10 marla house setups in Lahore sun, from a house with no AC (first row) to three 1.5 ton inverter ACs with an electric geyser (last row); fans, lights, fridge, freezer, TVs, pump, iron, washing machine and router are the same in every row

mistakes: Sizing from the bill of a house with no solar yet. The bill shows past units; the panels must also carry the running load of every AC you plan to run at the same time at noon, which for three ACs is the larger number.
Ordering a ten kW inverter with a five kW sanctioned load. The DISCO caps the net-metering system at the sanctioned load, so apply for the load extension first.
Sizing the battery for the whole list. The battery line assumes every appliance runs after dark; list only the night loads, and decide whether the AC is one of them, before you price a battery.

Counting inverter ACs at their rated watts for energy. An inverter AC cycles down once the room is cool, so the daily units use its average draw; the running load and the inverter size still use the rated watts.
Expecting rated panel watts every day. The performance ratio of {{d.pr|pct}} covers heat, dust, cable loss and cloud; the monthly units shown are a yearly average, not a sunny-day peak.
safety: A rooftop solar system of this size connects to the grid and to your house wiring at mains voltage, and its DC side runs at several hundred volts; have a licensed electrician and a DISCO-approved installer do the wiring, earthing, surge protection and net-metering connection.

faq.q: How many solar panels does a 10 marla house need?
faq.a: The typical 10 marla house above needs {{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w|int}} W, which is {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW and about {{out.roof_m2|int}} square metres of roof. With two 1.5 ton inverter ACs instead of three ACs it needs {{ex.1.out.panels|int}} panels.

faq.q: Is a 10 kW solar system enough for a 10 marla house with three ACs?
faq.a: Yes for three inverter ACs (two 1.5 ton and one 1 ton) with fans, lights, fridge, freezer, pump and washing machine: the house needs {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels and a {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter. Three 1.5 ton inverter ACs or non-inverter ACs move it to the next size; see the table.

faq.q: What solar system does a 10 marla house with two ACs need?
faq.a: With two 1.5 ton inverter ACs and the same fans, lights, fridge, freezer, pump and washing machine, the house needs {{ex.1.out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels ({{ex.1.out.panels|int}} panels) and an inverter of {{ex.1.out.inverter_kw|2}} kW, making about {{ex.1.out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month in Lahore.

faq.q: How many units does a 10 marla solar system make a month?
faq.a: About {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month for the {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW system in Lahore as a yearly average, against about {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day used by the house. Summer makes more and winter less; pick your city for its own sun yield.

faq.q: What sanctioned load do I need for a 10 marla solar system?
faq.a: At least the system size in kW, because the DISCO approves net metering only up to the sanctioned load. The running load of the default house is {{out.running_w|int}} W, and a sanctioned load of {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW or more comes with a time-of-use meter.

faq.q: Can a 10 marla solar system run ACs at night?
faq.a: Only from a battery or the grid. One 1.5 ton inverter AC with fans, lights, fridge and freezer for {{ex.2.out.night_hours|int}} hours needs about {{ex.2.out.battery_ah|int}} Ah of lithium at {{ex.2.out.battery_v|int}} V; without the AC the same night needs about {{ex.3.out.battery_ah|int}} Ah. Most houses keep the AC on the grid at night and size the battery for fans and lights.

faq.q: What is the price of a 10 marla solar system?
faq.a: Prices change with the exchange rate, so we do not print one. Compare quotes in Rs per watt for a complete {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW system with a {{out.inverter_kw|2}} kW inverter, including structure, cables, protection, installation and the net-metering application, and price the battery separately.
